signals.title: CAD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + JPY Outperformance
signals.text: CAD/JPY trades near 112.56 as JPY dominates G10 performance with a +1.420% weekly average across its peer group. The bilateral spread of 1.994% between the JPY leader and CAD laggard confirms a strong G10 theme, fueled by a bull steepener in the US yield curve (+41.7bp) and a -2.03% slide in the Nikkei 225. Despite a +125bp carry advantage favoring CAD, the JPY bid is supported by a positive ESI of +22.9, signaling sustained data beats. USD/JPY remains positioned below its SMA200 at 158.0, reinforcing the broader yen-strength regime. Risk: A rebound in risk sentiment and oil prices reverses CAD weakness, narrowing the bilateral G10 spread.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Skew + Geopolitical Risk
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 157.64, holding well below the SMA20/50 cluster near 161.88/161.25. The 25d risk reversal at -2.40 (Saxo, 1M tenor) reveals a strong put skew, indicating that the options market is paying a significant premium for JPY-strength protection. This bearish directional bias is compounded by reports of explosions in the Strait of Hormuz, which traditionally triggers safe-haven flows into the JPY. While the Fed-BoJ OIS carry differential remains wide at +268bp in favor of the USD, JPY COT positioning shows a massive net short of -124,575 contracts, leaving the pair vulnerable to a disorderly short-squeeze if geopolitical tensions escalate. Risk: Tensions in the Strait of Hormuz ease, allowing the carry-driven USD bid to reassert dominance above the SMA200 at 158.0.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Retail Divergence + Volatility Premium
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7059, maintaining its position above the SMA20/50/200 cluster (0.6986–0.7007). Myfxbook retail sentiment shows a 78% short bias, which directly diverges from the CFTC COT data where leveraged funds are net long +23,616 contracts. This extreme retail fade of an institutional trend often precedes further upside extensions. Meanwhile, the options market exhibits an elevated vol premium with IV at 11.5% against an HV30 of 6.1%, resulting in a +5.4% VRP. This suggests traders are aggressively hedging for volatility despite the steady uptrend. Risk: A break below the 0.6918 SMA200 invalidates the bullish institutional setup and triggers a retail-led reversal.

signals.title: NZD/USD — ESI Divergence + Positioning Extreme
signals.text: NZD/USD is trading at 0.5893, supported by a Strong Positive ESI of +24.4, the highest in the G10. However, COT positioning is at a bearish extreme with leveraged funds net short -30,606 and a long percentage of only 9.7%. RBNZ holds at 2.5%. While the real policy rate is accommodative at -1.56%, the persistent data beats suggest the market is underpricing NZD resilience. Risk: NZD/USD closes below the SMA50 at 0.5793, validating the heavy speculative short position.

signals.title: USD/CHF — Volatility Risk Premium Extreme
signals.text: USD/CHF at 0.8062 shows the most extreme volatility risk premium in the G10 space, with 1M implied volatility at 29.4% versus a realized HV30 of only 6.3%. This +23.1% VRP indicates the options market is pricing in a massive move that has not yet materialized in spot price action. Speculative positioning remains net short -11,635 contracts, while the pair holds below its SMA20 (0.8109) but above its SMA50 (0.8039). The extreme premium suggests institutional desks are hedging against a significant tail-risk event, likely tied to the ongoing Strait of Hormuz headlines. Risk: Volatility mean-reversion occurs without a spot break, leading to a rapid collapse in the IV premium.
